en.title: Ruag scandal: Swiss defense firm faces fraud investigation and civil claims
en.dek: Ruag faces fraud investigation, civil claims for €51 million, and scrutiny over military parts misappropriation.
facts: Ruag MRO released an investigative report by a law firm covering transactions from 2002, according to SRF.
The report identified compliance violations, structural control weaknesses, and a 'Business First' culture, according to SRF.
Ruag seeks €51 million in damages from ten former employees, according to SRF.
Defense Minister Martin Pfister said the case reveals serious misconduct, according to SRF.
Ruag alleges a former employee sold Leopard replacement parts to a Dutch state for €4.5 million, then resold them for €3 million, causing a €46.9 million loss, according to SRF.
body: According to SRF, Ruag MRO released an investigative report by a law firm. The report, published on 30 October 2026, examined transactions from 2002 onward, including Leopard-1 and Leopard-2 tank parts. The report identified compliance violations, structural control weaknesses, and a 'Business First' culture, according to SRF. It also noted that whistleblower warnings were not adequately followed.

According to SRF, Defense Minister Martin Pfister said the case reveals serious misconduct. Pfister announced that the Swiss government would investigate the company's own oversight. He said the investigation would involve an independent working group without company insiders. Pfister also said he would restore public trust through transparency and honesty.

According to SRF, Ruag has filed civil claims against ten former employees. The claims seek €51 million in damages and interest. Ruag alleges that a former employee sold Leopard replacement parts to a Dutch state for €4.5 million, then resold them for €3 million. Ruag claims a €46.9 million loss from that transaction.

According to SRF, the report identified at least 22 Leopard-2 gearboxes sold below market value between 2017 and 2022. Ruag claims a €4 million loss from those sales. The report said material stored for the Swiss Army was used for third‑party sales. Ruag says the material was not security‑critical and poses no risk.

According to SRF, Pfister said the Swiss government had received a U.S. commitment to supply Patriot system components. He said the U.S. ambassador, Callista Gingrich, informed him of positive procurement developments. Pfister said the U.S. government had approved direct procurement of Patriot systems from the manufacturer. The U.S. Congress has yet to approve the arrangement.
en.context: Ruag is a Swiss state‑owned defense contractor that supplies military equipment. The scandal involves alleged fraud, forged documents, and misappropriation of military parts. The investigation follows concerns that the company may have circumvented Swiss export rules.

problemsFixed: Use of loaded language such as "shocking" and "crimes" without attribution
Unsupported claims about specific financial losses not directly cited
Missing attribution for statements by Pfister and Ruag
Headline and dek not concise enough
Paragraphs contain four short sentences in a row
No clear attribution for whistleblower claims
No mention of the date of the investigative report
